sources_considered.why: Primary empirical research on reliability across model families; read_page returned readable text without a PARTIAL designation.
Primary theoretical analysis of unavoidable errors, with important limits on what its theorem establishes.

receipt.public_excerpt: larger and more instructable large language models may have become less reliable.

evidence_items.explanation: The experiments document persistent errors and sensitivity to phrasing across model families. They establish reliability problems, but do not isolate architecture as their necessary cause.

receipt.public_excerpt: we formalize the problem and show that it is impossible to eliminate hallucination in LLMs.

evidence_items.explanation: The formal result concerns computable models attempting to learn all computable ground-truth functions. That supports limits on universal correctness, but does not establish an ordinary unreliability rate or a defect specific to LLM architecture.

receipt.public_excerpt: Hallucinations need not be mysterious -- they originate simply as errors in binary classification.

evidence_items.explanation: This analysis identifies statistical limitations and incentives to guess, and proposes changes to evaluation incentives. It complicates an architecture-only explanation without demonstrating that all reliability problems can be eliminated.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not separate architectural necessity from data limitations and training incentives sufficiently to settle the attribution.
The impossibility result does not quantify practical reliability on a specified task distribution.
No agreed reliability threshold is supplied by the claim.
